segments.title: Ethics review process
segments.quote: Only the research on it, not the system itself. That distinction is the whole problem
segments.full_text: Interviewer: Did any part of this deployment come before your committee? Respondent: Only the research on it, not the system itself. That distinction is the whole problem. If a doctoral student wants to interview twelve people about the cameras, that comes to me and I will spend forty minutes on the consent form. The decision to install the cameras and point them at a hundred thousand people went through a procurement committee. Nobody thinks this is strange except the people who say it out loud.

codes.rationale: The decision to install the cameras was made by a procurement committee, not the ethics committee, indicating a lack of public or community engagement.

segments.title: Capacity and authority
segments.quote: Not as constituted. We have no authority over the city and no capacity if we did — we're eleven academics and an administrator, meeting six times a year, and we're already behind.
segments.full_text: Interviewer: Could your committee's remit cover deployments? Respondent: Not as constituted. We have no authority over the city and no capacity if we did — we're eleven academics and an administrator, meeting six times a year, and we're already behind. I mention the capacity because people propose expanding ethics review as though review were free.

codes.rationale: The committee lacks authority and capacity, limiting its ability to engage with broader stakeholders.
The respondent questions the assumption that ethics review is free and unburdened, but does not further reflect on the implications.

segments.title: Data protection impact assessment
segments.quote: More applications now include a data-protection impact assessment, which is progress.
segments.full_text: Interviewer: What have you seen change in the studies that do come to you? Respondent: More applications now include a data-protection impact assessment, which is progress. What I still almost never see is a plan for what the researcher will do if the finding is inconvenient to the funder. I've started asking for it. Roughly a third of applicants have no answer and about a fifth are visibly irritated that I asked.

codes.rationale: The inclusion of data-protection impact assessments suggests some level of engagement with ethical considerations.

segments.title: Lack of public voice
segments.quote: We have one lay member. One, out of twelve. She is excellent and she is also one person doing the work of a category. When she can't attend, the public perspective is simply absent from that meeting and we proceed anyway. We should not proceed anyway.

summary: The respondent demonstrates a weak engagement dimension, with a lack of public or community involvement in the decision-making process. There is some evidence of reflexivity in acknowledging the need for a plan in case of inconvenient findings, but this is not consistently applied. The committee's capacity and authority are limited, further hindering its ability to engage effectively. While there is a positive engagement in the form of data-protection impact assessments, the overall structure of the account suggests a need for more substantive engagement and reflexivity to ensure responsible innovation.
transcript:
Interview transcript A05 — Chair, university research ethics committee
Case: Port Calder adaptive traffic signal and pedestrian detection system  |  SYNTHETIC DATA — not a real interview
[Interviewer] Did any part of this deployment come before your committee?
[Respondent] Only the research on it, not the system itself. That distinction is the whole problem in one sentence. If a doctoral student wants to interview twelve people about the cameras, that comes to me and I will spend forty minutes on the consent form. The decision to install the cameras and point them at a hundred thousand people went through a procurement committee. Nobody thinks this is strange except the people who say it out loud.
[Interviewer] Could your committee's remit cover deployments?
[Respondent] Not as constituted. We have no authority over the city and no capacity if we did — we're eleven academics and an administrator, meeting six times a year, and we're already behind. I mention the capacity because people propose expanding ethics review as though review were free.
[Interviewer] What have you seen change in the studies that do come to you?
[Respondent] More applications now include a data-protection impact assessment, which is progress. What I still almost never see is a plan for what the researcher will do if the finding is inconvenient to the funder. I've started asking for it. Roughly a third of applicants have no answer and about a fifth are visibly irritated that I asked.
[Interviewer] Do affected communities have any voice in your process?
[Respondent] We have one lay member. One, out of twelve. She is excellent and she is also one person doing the work of a category. When she can't attend, the public perspective is simply absent from that meeting and we proceed anyway. We should not proceed anyway.
